scenarios.title: Second installation with its own history for a shared project: single apply and set planning are refused and its SQLite history is preserved

invariants.I3: na:no acknowledged hook input in this row; covered by F5/F6
invariants.I5: na:no unreachable-target step in this row; disclosure scan still runs on every step

scenarios.notes: Required second-machine history contract is a documented refusal: no merge or automatic join of an independent SQLite history into a shared project is attempted. Installation B keeps its history and queue. The refused single apply reports applied=true because apply mints the destination identity before the multi-machine check (docs/migration-operations.md describes apply as resolving or creating the destination identity itself); no hold, journal or SQLite change results. The ordering is tracked as the non-blocking Bug https://github.com/donadiosolutions/lcm/issues/1689; flip b-apply to applied=false if it is changed.

scenarios.notes: A real SQLite daemon alive across the cutover: activate and report exit 8 restart-required until it is stopped (#1683 fixed on main). Environment restriction: this daemon is started with the operator's PostgreSQL connection variables (LCM_POSTGRES_URL and LCM_POSTGRES_CA_FILE); a daemon started without them still gives exit 5 cutover-restart-contradiction because its observe route answers 503, tracked by https://github.com/donadiosolutions/lcm/issues/1696 and asserted by the pending row F10-no-target-env. After the restart the new daemon reports PostgreSQL, one bounded drain delivers an input acknowledged after the old daemon stopped (an administrator-owned trigger records the applied inbox row before the production prune, so the receipt is authenticated from that durable witness), and the SQLite project database is never written by either daemon.

invariants.I3: na:no acknowledged hook input in this row; covered by F5/F6

scenarios.notes: With only this row's owned role permission revoked (proved with has_schema_privilege and has_table_privilege), the product's backend diagnostic (lcm stats --pool --json) classifies the selected PostgreSQL as permission-denied and the daemon refuses to start by exiting on its own: explicit failure, no SQLite fallback. 'migration report' reads durable local evidence and does not probe the target, so it still reports the active selection. The row also asserts unchanged SQLite bytes, no new project database, PostgreSQL authority and recovery once the permission returns.
